mechanism_narrative: A rising month-over-month consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates accelerating inflation, which triggers central bank hawkishness and higher real interest rates, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.5%, it signals an aggressive monetary easing policy that lowers discount rates and stimulates corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strengthening labor market and robust supply chain, which together boost corporate profitability and investor confidence, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE falls by at least 0.2% and INDPRO rises by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC drops below 0.025 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-crisis recovery regime (defined by UNRATE < 8.5% and INDPRO > 90), housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signal sustained consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST is above its 12-month MA and the regime condition (UNRATE < 8.5% and INDPRO > 90) holds, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising month-over-month employment level (PAYEMS) indicates expanding labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS rises month-over-month, or the Rank IC remains below 0.025 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 100, it signals robust manufacturing activity and supply chain efficiency, which enhances corporate earnings visibility and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances when INDPRO > 100, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand across multiple sectors, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances when RSAFS and HOUST both rise by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC drops below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), a federal funds rate above 4.5% (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening that suppresses economic activity and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
